tldr: The causal target is the difference \(\theta(P)=q_1(P)-q_0(P)\) of latent marginal median responses under two stimulus implementations with a shared independent untreated shock. The sharp globally honest expected-length frontier is \(L(n,m,r)\asymp\rho(n,m,r)\), where \(\rho(n,m,r)=\min\{1,(\ell_{n,m}/n)^{5/16}+\min(r,1)m^{-1/2}\}\) and \(\ell_{n,m}=1+\log_+(n^{1/8}/\sqrt m)\). A finite data-only radius-blind outer confidence image has coverage at least \(0.9\) at every finite pair of sample sizes and attains this order with unconditional expected-length control. Legal product-experiment alternatives prove the matching lower bound. Scarce calibration produces a scanning logarithm with elbow \(m=n^{1/4}\): on the aligned slice the order is \((\log(en)/n)^{5/16}\) for \(m=2\) and \(n^{-5/16}\) for \(m\ge n^{1/4}\). The same interval attains every shrinking or fixed shape slice within a universal factor, so \(A(n,m)\asymp1\).
gap: Published unknown-error quantile rates concern one latent quantile. Adusumilli, Kurisu, Otsu and Whang (2020) also provide asymptotic deconvolution CDF and quantile bands, including repeated-measurement inference and a direct-error-sample extension. These results and the density bands of Kato, Sasaki and Ura (2021) do not characterize the finite-sample globally honest expected length of a two-arm marginal median difference across centered-shape slices under one shared shock sample.
